summary: Build practical humanitarian duty-of-care skills across OHS, wellbeing, safeguarding and security. Develop operational tools in this five-day course.
lede: The Duty of Care in Humanitarian Operations course shows how to bring occupational safety, staff wellbeing, field security and safeguarding into one evidence-based operating model. You will work with ISO 31000 risk assessments, ISO 45001 controls, ISO 45003 psychosocial hazard assessments, safeguarding and PSEA measures, and clear escalation routes for field security incidents. Through practical exercises, you will build multi-hazard risk registers, map controls, assess psychosocial exposure, design safeguarding referral pathways, use incident data to prioritise action and prepare leadership decision dashboards. The course also applies the Core Humanitarian Standard and IASC guidance to connect personnel protection with accountable, responsible service delivery.
audienceIntro: Humanitarian duty of care is designed for professionals who make or support safety, wellbeing, safeguarding and security decisions in high-risk operations. It suits experienced practitioners and managers who need an integrated framework, while remaining accessible to professionals moving into cross-functional duty-of-care responsibilities.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to humanitarian programme delivery, field coordination, HR, safeguarding, occupational safety or security operations. No programming is required. Basic familiarity with incident reporting, risk registers and organisational policies will help you contribute effectively, but the course introduces the integrated duty-of-care model from first principles. Depth: ISO 31000, ISO 45001, ISO 45003, CHS and IASC materials receive operational application through exercises. Mental health clinical practice, security intelligence analysis and digital dashboard automation remain conceptual or guided application topics rather than advanced implementation.
